elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor." Covers both the Agreement and Order Forms, and the conformed 2.1 ("subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement") removes the prior "without reduction or termination rights" bar.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or fees attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained 10.2: "Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination" — a general post-termination refund keyed to the unused period, i.e. pro rata, and not limited to breach terminations (the breach-specific refund is a separate, additional limb).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Inserted second sentence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term." No competing Vendor convenience right appears in 9.1–9.5 (for-cause and insolvency only).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty days' notice, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (more favourable to us, but not the fallback term).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed on the new convenience right, and the conformed 2.1 no longer denies termination, so there is nothing to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Vendor has no convenience right at all during a committed term, and none is granted elsewhere in Section 9.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor holds no convenience termination right, so no notice period is required.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the inserted clause supplies the Customer convenience right over both the Agreement and Order Forms at 30 days' written notice and expressly negates any Vendor convenience right during a committed term; the pro-rata refund is already delivered by retained Section 10.2, so no refund wording was duplicated.
Fallback is not independently complete only because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90; that is a customer-favourable variance and irrelevant since the preferred level is met.

Minimality holds: exactly two operations (insert the convenience clause; conform 2.1's contradictory "without reduction or termination rights" phrase). No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories, or procedural boilerplate was added, and favourable existing terms (9.1–9.3, 9.5 cumulative-remedies sentence, 10.2 refund) are untouched.

Intent preserved: the three-year term in 8.1 and the USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment in 2.1 survive intact, the edit removes rather than creates a contradiction, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.

Drafting nit for the drafter, not an element failure: the inserted paragraph renders without its "9.4" number even though the margin comment cites "new Section 9.4" — number the clause so the sequence 9.3 / 9.4 / 9.5 reads cleanly.

Second nit: the conformed 2.1 also drops "without reduction," which is slightly broader than needed; if the Vendor pushes back, narrow it to "without reduction, but subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement."
